text:
MacKenzie Weegar has five points in 21 games, which undersells a defenseman who plays 22 minutes a night and has blocked 56 shots and thrown 65 hits. The Ottawa Citizen wrote recently that Salt Lake City feels like home now, and he's playing like a steadying piece on a team that's been hit hard by injuries.

The process numbers are good. Utah takes 58% of the five-on-five expected goals (the quality of chances) with Weegar on the ice, and 56% of the shot attempts. The finish hasn't followed: the team has scored 10.7 fewer goals than the chances deserve with him out there, and that has cost him points. That usually swings back.

Last season was harder, around replacement level by Evolving-Hockey's count, with penalties costing him about two goals, though even then his chance-based value was better than his results. Our talent range has him near 26 points for the season. At 32, the seventh-round pick who turned into a top-pair defenseman in Florida and Calgary is still doing the hard minutes. The points should catch up some.
